# @wthek/express-middleware

> Production-safe Express.js error-handling middleware for `http-error-kit`.

## Overview
`@wthek/express-middleware` catches `KitHttpError` and `KitGeneralError` instances thrown in Express routes and automatically responds with the matching HTTP status code and structured JSON error payload. It protects against `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT` crashes, supports custom loggers, and optionally formats unknown exceptions.

## Installation
```bash
npm install @wthek/express-middleware http-error-kit http-response-status-code
```

## Quick Start
```typescript
import express from "express";
import { KitExpressMiddleware } from "@wthek/express-middleware";
import { BadRequestError, NotFoundError } from "http-error-kit";

const app = express();

app.get("/api/users/:id", (req, res) => {
  if (!req.params.id) {
    throw new BadRequestError("User ID is required");
  }
  throw new NotFoundError("User not found");
});

// IMPORTANT: Register AFTER all routes
app.use(KitExpressMiddleware({ log: true, handleUnknownErrors: true }));

app.listen(3000);
```

## API Reference

### `KitExpressMiddleware(options?: IKitExpressMiddlewareOptions)`
Returns an Express 4-argument error-handling middleware: `(error, req, res, next) => void`.

#### Options (`IKitExpressMiddlewareOptions`)
- `log` (`boolean | ((error: unknown, req: Request) => void)`, default: `false`):
  When `true`, logs via `console.error`. When a function is provided, calls custom logger.
- `handleUnknownErrors` (`boolean`, default: `false`):
  When `true`, catches non-Kit errors and returns a 500 JSON response instead of forwarding to Express's default HTML handler.

## Safety Rules for AI Agents
1. Always place `app.use(KitExpressMiddleware(...))` after all route definitions.
2. In async Express handlers, always forward errors via `next(err)` or throw in Express 5.
3. Throw errors directly from `http-error-kit` (e.g., `throw new BadRequestError(...)`).
